correctness.rationale: For all dimensions and positive finite heat-mixture measures with positive-time mass, the one-bit tensor heat kernel gives a convolution squared-kernel W. Its Walsh levels are explicit positive double integrals; the strict gap is the integral of products containing (1-e^-2s)(1-e^-2t)/2, positive on positive-mass time pairs. The Rademacher fourth-moment identity and Parseval yield exact variance and equality only at the unique top-degree character. The proof covers boundary conditions, normalization, and every two-sign assignment. The included stdlib verifier executed 9,685 exact-rational assertions, and finite checks are not used as universal proof.

originality.rationale: The inspected 2023 source gives variance for an arbitrary fixed partition but does not solve its global two-partition minimization; 2020 and 2013 sources give deterministic or hierarchical coloring methods. The new argument diagonalizes the Hadamard square of every positive hypercube heat mixture, establishes strict ordering over all Walsh degrees and obtains a unique global minimum, exact value, and quantitative excess for every sign assignment. The nearest owned prior claim is for shifted even cycles only. Search non-hits are not treated as proof of publication uniqueness, and a not-fully-read related article remains an explicit risk.

value.rationale: Coloring to avoid nearest-neighbor interactions competes with long-range within-color interactions. The exact all-coloring optimality for every positive heat-mixture filter resolves this tradeoff on the hypercube and yields a nonzero quantitative variance gap, a naturally useful guarantee for one-random-probe-per-color trace estimation. The application and object are motivated by the graph-coloring stochastic probing framework rather than an arbitrary low-dimensional slice.
